content: 1. Sulfamethoxazole and Aminobenzoate Potassium: Aminobenzoate potassium reduces the efficacy of sulfamethoxazole through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination should be avoided, or an alternative drug should be used. 2. Sulfamethoxazole and Aminolevulinic Acid (Oral): Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Additionally, avoid administering other phototoxic drugs with oral aminolevulinic acid during the perioperative period (24 hours). 3. Sulfamethoxazole and Aminolevulinic Acid (Topical): Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs through pharmacodynamic synergism. Each drug may enhance the photosensitizing effects of the other. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 4. Sulfamethoxazole and Amiodarone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 5. Sulfamethoxazole and Antithrombin Alfa: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of antithrombin alfa by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 6. Sulfamethoxazole and Antithrombin III: Sulfamethoxazole enhances the effects of antithrombin III by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 7. Sulfamethoxazole and Argatroban: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of argatroban by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 8. Sulfamethoxazole and BCG Vaccine (Live): Sulfamethoxazole reduces the efficacy of the BCG vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 9. Sulfamethoxazole and Bemiparin: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of bemiparin by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 10. Sulfamethoxazole and Bivalirudin: Sulfamethoxazole enhances the effects of bivalirudin by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 11. Sulfamethoxazole and Dalteparin: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of dalteparin by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 12. Sulfamethoxazole and Disopyramide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 13. Sulfamethoxazole and Enoxaparin: Sulfamethoxazole enhances the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 14. Sulfamethoxazole and Erdafitinib: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels or effects of erdafitinib by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 15. Sulfamethoxazole and Fondaparinux: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of fondaparinux by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 16. Sulfamethoxazole and Heparin: Sulfamethoxazole enhances the effects of heparin by decreasing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 17. Sulfamethoxazole and Ibutilide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 18. Sulfamethoxazole and Indapamide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 19. Sulfamethoxazole and Mefloquine: Mefloquine increases the toxicity of sulfamethoxazole by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 20. Sulfamethoxazole and Methenamine: This combination is contraindicated as it may form an insoluble precipitate in the urine, reducing the efficacy of both agents. 21. Sulfamethoxazole and Methotrexate: Sulfamethoxazole increases the toxicity of methotrexate by competing for plasma protein binding. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Elevated methotrexate concentrations may increase the risk of toxicity, such as bone marrow suppression. 22. Sulfamethoxazole and Methyl Aminolevulinate: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs through pharmacodynamic synergism. Each drug may enhance the photosensitizing effects of the other. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 23. Sulfamethoxazole and Pentamidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 24. Sulfamethoxazole and Pexidartinib: Both drugs inhibit gastrointestinal absorption when administered orally. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Pexidartinib may also cause hepatotoxicity, so avoid co-administration with other hepatotoxic agents. 25. Sulfamethoxazole and Phenindione: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of phenindione by reducing its metabolism and through plasma protein binding competition. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 26. Sulfamethoxazole and Pimozide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 27. Sulfamethoxazole and Pretomanid: Co-administration increases the toxicity of both drugs. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity. Avoid alcohol and other hepatotoxic agents during pretomanid therapy. 28. Sulfamethoxazole and Procainamide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 29. Sulfamethoxazole and Propranolol: Sulfamethoxazole increases the effects of propranolol by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Sulfamethoxazole and Quinidine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 31. Sulfamethoxazole and Sotalol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 32. Sulfamethoxazole and Tretinoin (Oral and Topical): Co-administration increases phototoxicity due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 33. Sulfamethoxazole and Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Sulfamethoxazole reduces the efficacy of the typhoid vaccine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 34. Sulfamethoxazole and Amantadine: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of amantadine by impairing renal clearance, leading to higher plasma concentrations. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Sulfamethoxazole and Amitriptyline: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 36. Sulfamethoxazole and Amoxapine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Sulfamethoxazole and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Sulfamethoxazole and Aspirin: Co-administration may enhance the effects of one drug by displacing the other from plasma protein binding sites. Use caution and monitor closely. The risk is low with low-dose aspirin. 39. Sulfamethoxazole and Estradiol/Estrogens: Sulfamethoxazole decreases the levels or effects of oral estrogens by altering intestinal flora. The risk of contraceptive failure is low. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Sulfamethoxazole and Cyclosporine: Co-administration increases the risk of nephrotoxicity and/or ototoxicity. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Sulfamethoxazole and Dapsone (Topical): Sulfamethoxazole increases the systemic exposure of dapsone and its metabolites, potentially inducing methemoglobinemia. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Sulfamethoxazole and Digoxin: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of digoxin by altering intestinal flora and through renal tubular competition. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Sulfamethoxazole and Dofetilide: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 44. Sulfamethoxazole and Dolasetron: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Sulfamethoxazole and Dronabinol: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of dronabinol by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Sulfamethoxazole and Dronedarone: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Sulfamethoxazole and Erythromycin (Various Forms): Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 48. Sulfamethoxazole and Fluconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 49. Sulfamethoxazole and Fluoxetine: Fluoxetine increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Sulfamethoxazole and Glimepiride/Glipizide/Glyburide: Sulfamethoxazole increases the levels of these drugs through plasma protein binding competition and by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Sulfamethoxazole and Haloperidol: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Sulfamethoxazole and Imatinib: Imatinib increases the levels of sulfamethoxazole by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Sulfamethoxazole and Imidapril: Co-administration increases the risk of hyperkalemia due to pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Sulfamethoxazole and Itraconazole/Ketoconazole: Both drugs prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
